description: Catalogue of Tycho Brahe's astrological practice: natal horoscopes for Danish royals, astrological judgments for Rudolf II, the meteorological diarium, and the astrological practice of the Hven press.

items.title: Horoscope of Christian IV
items.subject: Christian IV of Denmark
items.subject_role: Future King of Denmark; Frederik II's son
items.autograph_note: Autograph original lost; survives in multiple scribal copies
items.note: Cast by Tycho at the order of Frederik II when Prince Christian (the future Christian IV) was born. The nativity text is on tekstnet.dk. Six copies survive at KB; NKS 296 is a 17th-c. German-language Urtheil version.

surviving_copies.note: Copy; no individual record traced in the KB online catalogue (July 2026)

items.title: Horoscope of Prince Ulrik
items.subject: Prince Ulrik of Denmark
items.note: Autograph natal horoscope for Prince Ulrik, cast in 1579. GKS 1822 is in Tycho's own hand and bound in green velvet — a presentation object.

items.title: Horoscope of Duke Hans
items.subject: Duke Hans (Hans the Younger) of Denmark
items.note: Natal horoscope for the youngest Danish prince; partly autograph. Bound in green velvet, matching the Ulrik horoscope — probably produced at the same time as a royal commission.

items.title: Iudicium astrologicum huius geniturae
items.subject: Unknown
items.note: Astrological judgement of a nativity; subject unidentified. Vienna, ÖNB Cod. 10689/29. 4 leaves. Among Tycho's Prague papers.

items.title: Primae lineae germanicae alicuius genethliaci
items.subject: Unknown
items.note: German draft of a nativity; subject unidentified; attribution uncertain. 37 leaves. Vienna, ÖNB Cod. 10689/36.

items.title: Stellarum inerrantium Restitutionis Appendix
items.subject: Rudolf II, Holy Roman Emperor
items.autograph_note: Scribal apograph with autograph dedication inscription by Tycho
items.note: A unique supplement to the 1004-star catalogue restitution: 36 star positions adapted to Emperor Rudolf II's nativity as a deliberate act of Habsburg adulation. Found ONLY in Cod. 10707 — the longest of the three copies (31 leaves). Autograph dedication inscription by Tycho: 'Illustri & Generoso Domino RVDOLPHO CORADVCIO ... ddt Tycho Brahe Anno 1600 Mense Martio'. First published by Dreyer (TBOO III, pp. 379-389).

surviving_copies.note: Unique apograph with Tycho's autograph dedication to Corraduz

items.title: Responsio ad quaestionem astrologicam Caesareae Maiestati
items.title_latin: Responsio ad questionem an iuxta astrologiam Caesareae Maiestati
items.subject: Rudolf II, Holy Roman Emperor
items.note: Tycho's reply to an astrological question put to his Imperial Majesty. Digitised. Vienna, ÖNB Cod. 10689/50.

items.title: Astrological judgment on the new star (or comet) of 1572
items.title_latin: Quae genera eventuum portendat crinita a. 1572
items.subject: The new star or comet of 1572
items.note: Astrological judgment on what events the nova/comet of 1572 portends. 8 bundled items; ties to the De nova stella thread. Vienna, ÖNB Cod. 10689/41-46. The ÖNB title's word 'crinita' — the standard Latin epithet for a comet — leaves the object's identification open.

items.title: Meteorological diary (1582-97)
items.subject: Weather and atmospheric observations
items.note: The meteorological-astrological diary kept daily at Uraniborg 1582-97. Combines weather observations with the astrological theory that planetary configurations govern atmospheric conditions. Printed 1876 from the Vienna original as an appendix to the Royal Danish Academy's Collectanea Meteorologica (prepared by Paul la Cour); the tekstnet edition gives the preface fragment.

items.title: Diarium astrologicum et metheorologicum (1586)
items.subject: Meteorological-astrological predictions for 1586
items.autograph_note: By Tycho's assistant Morsing under his imprimatur
items.note: The first true book printed on Tycho's Hven press (Nielsen LN 1170). Authored by Tycho's assistant Elias Olsen Morsing but issued under Tycho's editorial imprimatur and with his preface. A practical almanac combining astronomical tables with astrological weather predictions.

items.title: Astrologia — En Elementisch oc Jordisch Astrologia (1591)
items.subject: Popular meteorological-natural astrology
items.autograph_note: By Peder Jacobsen Flemløs; Tycho wrote the preface
items.note: The ONLY Danish-language book from the Uraniborg press (Nielsen LN 606). By Tycho's assistant Flemløs; Tycho wrote the preface. A popular work explaining natural/meteorological astrology in the vernacular for a Danish readership.

items.title: Horoscope of Titan (Erik Lange) in Urania Titani
items.subject: Erik Lange
items.subject_role: Sophie Brahe's fiancé; Tycho's friend; pseudonym Titan in the Uraniborg circle
items.autograph_note: Embedded in the poem text; reconstructed from verse by Ove von Späth (appendix in Zeeberg 1994)
items.note: The first horoscope Urania/Sophie examines in the poem: she tries to find proof of Titan's constancy in the stars, but the same configuration that promises eloquence and love undermines it. Mercury at the ascendant (18°56' Gemini) near Venus (17°6' Gemini) signifies natural eloquence and charm — but Mercury is retrograde and in House 1 without a stabilising benefic, which in classical astrology signals inconstancy and unreliability. Tycho constructs the literary argument so that Urania's attempt to reassure herself fails: the very planets she invokes as tokens of Titan's fidelity simultaneously expose his instability. Birth date: 27 May 1554; ASC 14°24' Gemini; MC 3°10' Aquarius.

surviving_copies.note: Primary witness (V); horoscope embedded in poem lines 235–270 (approx.)

items.title: Horoscope of Urania (Sophie Brahe) in Urania Titani
items.subject: Sophie Brahe
items.subject_role: Tycho's sister; alchemist and astrologer; pseudonym Urania in the Uraniborg circle
items.autograph_note: Embedded in the poem text; two reconstructions (A and B) by Ove von Späth correspond to Sophie's two disputed birth dates (Zeeberg 1994, appendix)
items.note: Sophie Brahe's birth date is uncertain — either 22 September 1556 (reconstruction A: ASC 29°58' Virgo, MC 29°57' Gemini; Sun 8°49' Libra in H1) or 24 August 1559 (reconstruction B: ASC 9°42' Virgo, MC 1°30' Gemini; Sun 9°42' Virgo conjunct ASC). Both reconstructions give a Virgo ascendant, consistent with the poem's characterisation of Urania as precise, discriminating, scientifically gifted, and devoted to service. The Virgo ascendant is the load-bearing astrological signature regardless of which date is correct.

surviving_copies.note: Primary witness (V); horoscope embedded in poem

items.title: Horoscope of Tage Thott in Urania Titani
items.subject: Tage Thott
items.subject_role: Sophie Brahe's only child, her son by Otte Thott of Eriksholm (d. 1588); courier between Sophie and Erik Lange in the poem's narrative
items.autograph_note: Embedded in the poem text; reconstructed from verse by Ove von Späth (appendix in Zeeberg 1994)
items.note: Tage Thott (born 28 May 1580) appears in the poem as the bearer of news from the outside world — a structural role that occasions a brief horoscope. ASC 8°3' Leo; MC 12°17' Aries. The Leo ascendant signals nobility and a commanding nature; the poem uses this to characterise him as a trusted young nobleman whose loyalty to Sophie is beyond question. He was the only child of Sophie Brahe and her first husband, Otte Thott of Eriksholm, whose death in 1588 left Sophie the widow the poem depicts.

surviving_copies.note: Primary witness (V); horoscope embedded in poem

items.title: Horoscope of Apollo (Tycho Brahe) in Urania Titani
items.title_latin: Genethliacon Apollinis / Tychonis Brahe in 'Urania Titani'
items.subject: Tycho Brahe
items.subject_role: Author of the poem; Sophie's brother; pseudonym Apollo in the Uraniborg circle
items.autograph_note: Embedded in the poem text; Tycho writes his own horoscope in Urania's voice — a remarkable act of self-characterisation under the veil of the epistolary fiction
items.note: The most remarkable of the four: Tycho writes his own horoscope in the voice of his sister, as a counterweight to Titan's unstable chart. ASC 22°32' Aquarius; Mars 11°1' Aries in House 1 (Mars in its own sign and angular house: martial courage and mastery of precision instruments); MC 17°37' Sagittarius. The Aquarius ascendant aligns Apollo with intellectual vision and unconventional genius. This reconstruction agrees with the known Tycho birth data (14 December 1546), confirming the poem's internal astrological consistency and lending additional authority to the Tycho authorship case.

surviving_copies.note: Primary witness (V); horoscope embedded in poem
